scope: Topic-level draft only; subtopic objectives and missing foundations must be reviewed before learner routing.

dependencies.rationale: Arithmetic operations on integers and fractions are needed before multi-operation expressions.
Factors, multiples and divisibility support common-factor and common-multiple methods.
Ratios require equivalent fractions and arithmetic with a common multiplier.
A percentage expresses a ratio with denominator 100.
The arithmetic mean uses sums and division by the item count.
Profit, loss and discount rates require an explicitly chosen percentage base.
Interest is a percentage of principal per stated time unit.
Compare fixed-principal interest with interest on an updated balance.
Work problems use rates and reciprocal time per unit work.
Inlet and outlet rates combine using the same work-rate model with signs.
Speed is a ratio of distance to time; proportional changes and units matter.
Train problems add object length and relative speed to distance-rate-time.
Ground speed combines the boat's still-water speed with signed stream speed.
Mixture concentrations are weighted amounts divided by total amount.
Alligation derives from a weighted average, rather than an unexplained cross-rule.
Algebraic manipulation depends on arithmetic operations and signed quantities.
Area and volume formulas require the dimensions and properties of the shapes.
Right-triangle ratios require perpendicular, hypotenuse and angle concepts.
Angles of elevation and depression use right-triangle ratios.
Coordinate relations and line equations require signed values and algebra.
Coordinate geometry connects numerical positions to geometric distances and shapes.
Mean and deviations build on sum and count; median/mode need separate instruction.
Chart questions require ratios, percentage bases and percentage change.
Tabular and chart comparisons often require total-to-average conversion.
Set membership, inclusion, disjointness and distinct witnesses explain categorical conclusions.
